research_rationale:
EO:11657 (signed 1972-03-22; 37 FR 6043 (Federal Register of March 24, 1972)) is a single-command order. The order exempts C. Everett Spangler, a member of the Federal Farm Credit Board, from compulsory retirement for age under subsection (c) of section 8335 of title 5, United States Code, until April 1, 1974. The order recites that he reached the age of 70 on February 4, 1972, and adds "This order shall be effective March 1, 1972." The register title spells his given name Everette; the text spells it Everett. Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing in jobs/fr-originals; its number, date and subject agree with the census register. Inventory: I confirm the dossier's one clause, which carries the recitals and the sole operative sentence; the text holds no other command, condition or proviso. The exemption ends by its own terms on 1974-04-01: the order's end date is quoted from the held text as "April 1, 1974", recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of that day); the exclusive reading, that it ends when April 1, 1974 begins, is the alternative a reviewer should see (owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on until-dates). Whether Spangler left office before the stated date is in no held source and is not asserted; the stated date is the latest day the exemption could operate. Searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes (all complete, none with a coverage warning): the U.S. Code search (release point 119-121, citations of the order by number in statute text and notes; edition current through 2026-10-09) recorded 0 hits; the eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 with GovInfo CFR bulk XML recorded 0 hits; the Federal Register catalog disposition-note search (1937 onward) recorded 0 hits for this order. I also searched every held order text (the Cruden held-text search, 33118 readable files) for the order's number; the only held texts that cite it are its own Federal Register printing. A held-text search of the person's name finds only that person's own exemption orders (this order) and unrelated matches.
